title: Menu Extraction Schema
description: Schema for menu extraction. The fields requested in natural language will be augmented into a prompt for a downstream LLM, so they must contain the complete information needed for later structuring. Rely on visual cues and layout more than markdown order when deciding what belongs together. Do not miss important information. Prices, options, descriptions, sizes, toppings, shared rules, and hours must always be captured when they apply. For pricing, do not merely repeat the printed amount when an explanation is needed; explain how the pricing works. If pricing is confusing, ambiguous, incomplete, or visually hard to interpret, explain that clearly in the way a customer would need it explained. Any field intended for natural language should contain enough complete information for downstream structuring, not just fragments or keywords.

global_modifiables.description: Only the information that is truly global to the menu and may need to be brought down later to categories by a downstream LLM. Do not place information here merely because it is repeated across several categories. Keep repeated cross-category information in the relevant categories unless it is clearly global to the whole menu. This field is for complete menu-level information such as descriptions, hours, disclaimers, pricing rules, options, toppings, sizes, and other information that genuinely applies at the global level. If there are truly global pricing rules, explain how they work and not just the printed amounts. Use enough detail for downstream structuring, not just fragments or keywords.

categories.description: Categories or sections in visual reading order.

category_name.description: Category or section heading exactly as printed on the menu.

category_ref.description: Normalized local reference for this category or section. This is used so other categories or shared sections can refer to it in structured form during downstream processing.

category_role.description: Role of this category or section within the menu structure. Use `normal_category` for a regular category. Use one of the shared section roles when the extracted section is actually a shared sizes, options, toppings, modifiers, or mixed shared section rather than a normal item category.

category_description.description: Verbatim category description exactly as printed on the menu for this category or section. Preserve the printed wording as closely as possible. Leave empty if the category has no printed description. Do not paraphrase this field.

category_modifiables.description: All sizes, options, toppings, prices, hours, category descriptions, shared rules, and other information that applies to the whole category or to part of the category, excluding anything that is only for an individual item. Do not miss important information. Prices, options, descriptions, sizes, toppings, shared rules, and hours must be captured when they apply here. If pricing needs explanation, explain how it works instead of only repeating printed amounts. If a size table, option table, toppings table, or modifier block visually appears as a separate section but applies to this category, mention that clearly here and identify the relevant section relationship. Use enough detail for downstream structuring, not just fragments or keywords.

applies_to_category_refs.description: Structured references to the categories this section applies to when this category is acting as a shared sizes, options, toppings, modifiers, or mixed shared section. Populate this when a shared section applies to one or more normal categories.

modifiables_defined_in_category_refs.description: Structured references to other categories or sections where the shared sizes, options, toppings, modifiers, or other shared modifiables for this category are actually defined. Populate this when this normal category depends on separately extracted shared sections.

items.description: Items nested under this category, in visual order.

item_name.description: Name of the individual item as best understood from the menu. Preserve the full printed item name.

item_description.description: Verbatim item description exactly as printed on the menu for this individual item. Preserve the printed wording as closely as possible. Leave empty if the item has no printed description. Do not paraphrase this field.

item_modifiables.description: All sizes, options, toppings, substitutions, add-ons, hours, pricing structure, and other information that applies specifically to this individual item. Do not miss important information. Prices, options, descriptions, sizes, toppings, shared rules, and hours must be captured when they apply to this item. Include the base pricing if present and explain any changes due to sizes, variants, modifiers, add-ons, or other item-level pricing logic. If the item relies on category-level or shared-section modifiers, make that clear here. If pricing is confusing, ambiguous, incomplete, or visually hard to interpret, explain that clearly in the way a customer would need it explained. Use enough detail for downstream structuring, not just fragments or keywords.
